newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain export commitments down on last year.
newsitem.headline: EU grain export commitments down on last year.

text.p: Latest European Union figures show grain export commitments between July 1 and November 5 were 10.5 percent below year-ago levels, mostly because of a steep fall in wheat sales, member-country officials said on Friday.
The figures, based on delivered export certificates, showed commercial wheat exports sharply lagging on last year at 2.698 million tonnes against 3.598 million.
Flour export commitments reached 1.972 million tonnes, down from 2.668 million during the same period last year.
Commercial barley exports, however, jumped to 1.996 million tonnes from 940,000 tonnes during the same period last year, helped by sales to Saudi Arabia.
Malt exports fell to 1.723 million tonnes from 1.907 million.
Commercial oats commitments reached 183,000 tonnes. The EU made no oat sales during the same period last year.
Since November 5, the EU has granted 350,500 tonnes of soft wheat, 133,500 tonnes of barley and 18,693 tonnes of rye exports through its weekly grain tender system.
